h1: The 4 Best GE Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four GE microwaves, from a 1150W countertop model to over-the-range units, compared on wattage, capacity and venting.
summary: The GE 1150W countertop microwave is our top pick for most kitchens. The GE 30 inch over-the-range unit is the sensible choice if you are replacing a built-in, the 1.9 cu. ft. model gives the strongest vent, and the GE Profile low profile suits tight cabinet clearance.
intro: The most common GE buying mistake is shopping by wattage alone. A countertop unit and an over-the-range unit can share a wattage figure and still be wrong for the same kitchen, because one needs counter space and the other needs a vent path and a mounting plate.

We reviewed GE's current listings and ranked four that cover the real decision points: countertop versus over-the-range, capacity, and exhaust strength. The ranking is based on listed specs, so check the install details for your own kitchen before ordering.

products.name: GE Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A high-wattage countertop GE with no installation fuss.
products.description:
This GE countertop model is listed at 1150 watts with a 1.6 cu. ft. cavity. Plug it in and it works, which makes it the simplest GE to own.

It ranks first because 1150 watts is the highest cooking power in this group, and it avoids the venting and mounting work the over-the-range units require. The tradeoff is that it eats counter space and offers no hood vent.

It suits renters and anyone who wants fast heating without touching the wall. Note that the listing gives few extra features, so check the control panel details before buying.
products.idealFor: Renters and apartment cooks who want strong, simple reheating.
products.skipIf: You want a hood vent and light above your stove.

products.name: GE 30" Over-the-Range Microwave
products.verdict: The standard replacement for a 30 inch built-in microwave.
products.description:
This 30 inch over-the-range GE offers 1.6 cu. ft. of space, 1000 watts, a 300 CFM hood vent and LED lighting. It frees the counter and replaces your range hood.

It sits below the countertop model because cooking power drops to 1000 watts and install work is required. The 300 CFM vent also trails the 400 CFM options below.

Choose it when you have a matching 30 inch opening. The caveat is that it needs mounting and a venting plan, so measure first.
products.idealFor: Homeowners replacing an existing 30 inch over-range microwave.
products.skipIf: You rent or have no wall-mounted bracket.

products.name: GE Over the Range Microwave Oven with 1.9 cu. ft. Capacity
products.verdict: The biggest cavity and stronger vent for busy stoves.
products.description:
This over-the-range GE lists 1.9 cu. ft. of capacity, 1000 cooking watts, convertible venting, 400 CFM airflow and 10 power levels.

It ranks below the 30 inch 1.6 cu. ft. model because bigger is not always better in a tight opening, but its stronger vent and larger cavity win for frequent cooks. Convertible venting lets you route air out or recirculate it.

Buy it if you cook large dishes and want better smoke control. Confirm your cabinet depth and venting before ordering.
products.idealFor: Families cooking big dishes over a busy range.

products.name: GE Profile 30" Over-the-Range Low Profile Microwave
products.verdict: A shallower GE for tight spaces above the range.
products.description:
The Profile low profile lists 1.2 cu. ft. of capacity, 1000 watts, a 400 CFM hood vent and LED lighting in a 30 inch width.

It ranks last because the cavity is the smallest here, but it keeps the 400 CFM vent that the 1.6 cu. ft. model lacks. You trade space for a slimmer look.

It suits cooks with limited clearance who still want a strong vent. A 1.2 cu. ft. cavity may not fit a large plate.
products.idealFor: Kitchens with limited clearance above the range.
products.skipIf: You need to fit large dinner plates.

whatMatters.detail: A countertop unit plugs in and sits on your counter, while an over-the-range unit mounts above the stove and doubles as a vent. The wrong choice costs you either counter space or an installation. Check your wall for a mounting bracket and a standard 30 inch opening before buying.

Wattage is the power the microwave uses to heat food. Higher wattage cooks faster, and a 900 watt unit takes noticeably longer than a 1150 watt one. Look for the wattage in the product title or bullet list, not the marketing copy.

Capacity is the interior volume in cubic feet. Under 1.4 cu. ft. can struggle with a standard dinner plate, while 1.9 cu. ft. handles large dishes. Check the interior diameter if you plan to heat big plates.
CFM measures how much air the hood fan moves. A busy stove benefits from 400 CFM, while 300 CFM is acceptable for light cooking. Look for the figure and whether it vents out or recirculates.
Over-the-range models are typically 30 inches wide and need a minimum clearance above the burners. A low profile unit helps when you are tight. Measure the opening and the height before ordering.

faq.q: Can an over-the-range GE replace a countertop one?
faq.a: Only if you can mount it above the stove. It needs a bracket, an electrical outlet and a venting plan.

faq.q: What is the common mistake when buying a GE microwave?
faq.a: Ignoring width and clearance. Always measure the opening, since 30 inches is the usual over-range standard.

faq.q: Is the GE Profile worth it over the standard 30 inch model?
faq.a: It gives a stronger 400 CFM vent in a low profile body, but its 1.2 cu. ft. cavity is smaller than the 1.6 cu. ft. model.

faq.q: How do I set up convertible venting?
faq.a: The 1.9 cu. ft. GE supports both outside venting and recirculation, so choose based on your ductwork.

faq.q: How do I maintain an over-the-range GE?
faq.a: Wash or replace the grease filter regularly, and wipe the cavity after spills.

faq.q: Can a countertop GE heat large dishes?
faq.a: The 1150 watt model has a 1.6 cu. ft. cavity, which handles standard plates. Very large dishes may need the 1.9 cu. ft. unit.

finalTake: The GE 1150W countertop microwave is the best fit for most kitchens. If you are replacing a built-in, the GE 30 inch is the straightforward swap, and the 1.9 cu. ft. model is the pick for serious cooks.
